notes: Identity independently checked: supplied text has the title Revisiting the folk concept of intentionality: Replications of Malle and Knobe (1997), Chandrashekar and the named coauthors including Feldman, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology 102 (2022) 104372, and DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2022.104372. It is a published primary replication report with main article pp. 1–7 and supplementary materials, not an abstract-only excerpt or preregistration. No PDF was supplied; no layout rendering performed. Average inter-rater correlation r = .59; average rater–whole correlation r = .77. Table 2 also prints condition-specific inter-rater correlations .59, .59, .63, .56 and rater–whole correlations .77, .77, .79, .75. Exact coefficient not selected because supplied locator cannot distinguish the two r measures or condition strata. Inspected section 4.1 and the complete Table 2: they report average inter-rater and rater–whole correlations, ICC and alpha, including condition estimates, without p-values for these agreement measures. No candidate agreement r has a printed same-test p. Supplementary p. 17 p-values concern cross-sample correlations; ANOVA, t-test and mixed-model p-values concern condition differences and cannot be transferred. Authors explicitly support the original central argument of substantial agreement; this is their joint qualitative replication verdict, not significance-based inference. Footnote 6 (p. 4) bases main conclusions on Study 2; p. 6 cautions that Study 1 cannot support independent conclusions because of its small sample. No conversions or analytic N derivations. Original side and replication n are unassigned placeholders.
